title: Self-Anchored Temporal Filtering for LLM-Free Temporal-Aware Memory Retrieval

contributions.purpose: Enable temporal-aware memory retrieval without expensive LLM calls for time-constraint extraction.
contributions.mechanism: Self-Anchored Temporal Filtering (SATF) infers temporal relevance from the timestamp distribution of initial retrieval results using multi-peak Gaussian kernels weighted by reciprocal rank, soft-boosting temporally coherent items without hard filtering.
contributions.evaluation: Requires zero LLM calls / zero API cost while performing temporal filtering on LongMemEval.
contributions.source_quote: We propose SATF, a novel temporal filtering method that infers temporal relevance from retrieval distributions using multi-peak Gaussian kernels, requiring zero LLM calls.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate SATF improves temporal reasoning retrieval quality over LLM-based filtering.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluation on LongMemEval temporal reasoning queries, comparing against GPT-4o time-range filtering.
contributions.evaluation: +16.9% relative NDCG@10 improvement on temporal reasoning queries (0.584 to 0.683), outperforming GPT-4o time-range filtering across all metrics.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that SATF achieves +16.9% relative NDCG@10 improvement on temporal reasoning queries in LongMemEval, outperforming GPT-4o time-range filtering across all metrics.

contributions.purpose: Show SATF is safe to apply universally without harming non-temporal queries.
contributions.mechanism: Per-question-type analysis on LongMemEval measuring recall changes when SATF is applied to all query types.
contributions.evaluation: SATF improves all question types with maximum recall degradation of only -0.014 on non-temporal queries.
contributions.source_quote: We show that SATF improves all question types without degrading non-temporal queries, with maximum recall degradation of only -0.014.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work complements these approaches by providing an LLM-free temporal filtering mechanism that can be integrated into existing memory systems.
Our self-anchored approach differs by inferring temporal relevance from the retrieval distribution itself, without requiring explicit temporal parsing or LLM-based time extraction.

We build upon dense retrieval as our base layer, using Stella embeddings for initial semantic matching, and add temporal reranking as a lightweight post-processing step that preserves the efficiency benefits of dense retrieval while incorporating temporal awareness.
